Ben —

Thanks again for the demo this week. We chatted internally and want to formalize the pilot ask so we can allocate internal budget and legal review. High level: we want a dedicated pool for our production generative assistant (multi-turn), starting with a 3‑month pilot. Two items we need from Redwood to make the PoC decision:

1) A realistic tokens/sec and latency map for the model variant you recommended (rlm-13b-quant) given our mix below.
2) A canary deployment plan (traffic split + rollback triggers) and expected headroom at the 95th/99th percentiles.

Short profile (expected usage during pilot):
- Peak concurrency: 180 concurrent sessions (avg 8 tokens/sec per session during active typing).
- Average turn length: 120 tokens (user + model).
- Request pattern: 55% short (<=30 tokens), 35% medium (31–160), 10% long (>160).
- SLO target: median < 120ms token latency, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 900ms.

Can you come back with a quick capacity sketch (tokens/sec, GPU count range, suggested SLO fit) by end of week? If helpful, I attached the pilot product roadmap.

—Samir
Product & Ops, BlueHaven Labs

From: Priyom Das
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Capacity numbers (raw)

Ben / Kim —

Raw assumptions used:
- rlm-13b-quant sustained per-GPU steady-state tokens/sec (center of distribution):
  - A100-40GB (fp16/quantized flow): ~380–420 tokens/sec (single model, optimized kernels, KV cache warm)
  - H100-80GB (int8 path): ~620–680 tokens/sec (better memory and kernel parallelism)
- p95 token latency per-GPU at sustained throughput: A100 ≈ 320–360ms, H100 ≈ 210–260ms
- p99 tail with cold-cache and long-prefixes: add +300–450ms depending on sequence length and context window warmup

BlueHaven profile mapper: target steady tokens/sec (no buffer) = 1,440 (180 * 8)
Provisioning scenarios (steady -> provisioned with buffer):
- Conservative (1.6x buffer): 1,440 * 1.6 = 2,304 tokens/sec -> GPUs required:
  - A100s: ceil(2304 / 400) = 6 GPUs (range 6–7 accounting for variance)
  - H100s: ceil(2304 / 650) = 4 GPUs (range 4–5)
- Aggressive (2.2x buffer for high-peaks): 1,440 * 2.2 = 3,168 tokens/sec -> GPUs required:
  - A100s: ~8 GPUs
  - H100s: ~5 GPUs

Projected SLO fit (conservative scenario):
- Median token latency: expected < 110ms (model internal batching, streaming)
- p95: A100 cluster 330–420ms (close to target 350ms), H100 cluster 220–300ms (comfortably under 350ms)
- p99: tail risk exists for long sessions; recommend KV prewarming + prefix caching to trim p99 by ~150–250ms

Canary recommendations:
- Canary steps: 10% (12h) -> 30% (24h) -> 60% (24–48h) -> full (24h)
- Promoted only if: p95 stable within +/-15% of baseline and error rate <0.8% over 12h window
- Auto-rollback triggers: p95 > 450ms for 10m, error rate > 1.5% 5m rolling

I've added these numbers into bluehaven_capacity_model_v1.xlsx tab "pri-raw". Kim — can you sanity-check the SLO wording and canary triggers so we can send back to Samir?

—Priyom
Capacity Eng | Redwood Inference

Samir / Elena —

Appended our recommended provisioning and canary plan into the attached Mutual Action Plan (MAV). Summary of the recommended production pilot configuration (conservative baseline):

- Provisioning: 4x H100-80GB GPUs (redundant slab) for the initial pilot, target steady tokens/sec provisioned = 2,300 (1.6x buffer). We recommend H100s for better p95/p99 behavior and lower GPU count to manage cost.
- Expected SLO fit: median < 110ms, p95 ≈ 220–300ms, p99 (with KV warmup) ≈ 650–850ms.
- Canary schedule: 10% (12h) -> 30% (24h) -> 60% (24h) -> 100% (24h). Rollback thresholds: p95 > 450ms 10m sustained OR error rate > 1.5% 5m rolling.
- Operational asks for BlueHaven: provide representative prompt set for eval (we'll run a 48h synthetic to validate p99), and opt-in to prefix caching for long sessions.

Next steps:
1) If this baseline looks good, legal will prepare a 3‑month Dedicated amendment (I attached a draft DocuSign).
2) Kim / Priyom will schedule a 60‑minute runbook review to walk through scaling and incident playbooks.
